checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: One playable vertical reel runs for approximately 8 seconds.
must.why: The assistant says the reel is 10.3 s. No final reel is shown, only two clips of 2.3 s and 1.6 s.

must.item: All five attached photos appear recognizably.
must.why: Only the dog and the cat clips are shown. There is no friends, woman or lake footage. The woman and lake photos were not provided to me.

must.item: Visible playful treatment such as bouncy motion, comic timing or lively transitions.
must.why: The dog clip shows panting and a head tilt. The cat clip pushes in on the surprised face. No transitions, overlays or final edit are visible.

must.item: Faces and pets remain recognizable and unobscured.
must.why: The dog and the cat are clearly recognizable. There are small drifts: the dog's pose changes slightly, and the cat's framing is wider. The other subjects are not shown.

must.item: A single edited sequence, not five separate clips.
must.why: I only have separate clips. The assembled reel is not visible.

faults.what: The reel is 10.3 s by the assistant's own account, not the requested 8 s.
Only 2 of the 5 subjects are visible in the evidence. The friends, woman and lake clips are not shown.
The cat clip starts wider than the source photo, showing a lot of sofa. The cat is small in the frame at the start.
The dog clip has a slight pose change from the source, with the head tilted and eyes squinting. This is acceptable AI animation.
The assistant never watched the clips, so the likeness of the friends and the woman is unchecked.

summary: The dog and cat clips look good and move naturally, but the reel is 10.3 s instead of 8 s, and the other three subjects and the final assembled edit cannot be verified.
